newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris unaffected by transport workers strike.
newsitem.headline: Paris unaffected by transport workers strike.

text.p: A transport workers strike over wages and jobs failed to disrupt Paris metro and bus services on Friday, but a separate dispute slashed train services in southeastern France for a fifth day, transport officials said.
The Paris transport authority RATP said at mid-morning that traffic on the underground and suburban RER networks was normal despite the call for a strike to demand staff and pay increases.
RATP had earlier forecast that traffic would be cut by up to 20 percent at mid-morning and at the evening rush hour.
In Marseille, talks between the state rail company SNCF and striking workers broke down and the protesters were meeting to decide whether to stiffen their protest over proposed job cuts.
The five-day-old strike has slightly disrupted long-distance trains in the southeast, but up to 80 percent of regional trains have been cancelled. The high-speed TGV trains were unaffected.

The two most powerful SNCF unions have asked members to join a nationwide strike called for October 17 by civil service unions to press for a pay raises and protest against the centre-right government's plans to cut 6,000 jobs next year.
Railworkers led a crippling 24-day public sector strike late last year when Prime Minister Alain Juppe proposed ending early pension rights -- plans which have since been scrapped.

The concern this time is over programmed job cuts and a modernisation plan under which the government will take 125 billion francs ($25 billion) of debt off the loss-making SNCF by spinning it off into another state company which would also become owner of the track and other infrastructure.
Unions fear the plan could open the way to additional staff cuts or a possible privatisation of the SNCF.
